summary: This sermon explores koinonia, the Greek word for fellowship that describes one of the church's four core practices. The speaker argues that koinonia is far more than casual friendship—it is an all-in joint venture in Christ that encompasses divine fellowship through communion, sharing resources with those in need, mutual accountability, and shared mission. Using examples from Acts 2 and Philippians, the sermon shows how the early church practiced this deep commitment and calls the congregation to prioritize real relationships over idealized community.
key_points: Koinonia is putting belief into action through shared practice, not just gathering together
It includes fellowship with Christ through communion, sharing resources financially, and sharing in Christ's sufferings
Real community requires examination, repentance, forgiveness, and unity—not an idealized picture
Community is the primary means of grace where believers confess sins and hold each other accountable
The example of Blazing Hope Ranch demonstrated koinonia through united service and shared mission
big_idea: True Christian community (koinonia) is an all-in joint venture in Christ that requires shared ownership of the mission, vulnerability with one another, and prioritizing real relationships over personal preferences to fulfill the church's purpose together.
title: We Are the Church: Koinonia
